### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **38** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/register-sso-provider.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx`  _(via firstName (symbol, a field of const object SAML_STANDARD_CLAIMS))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via providerId (symbol, a field of interface SamlProviderScope))_
- `content/docs/deployment/troubleshooting.mdx`  _(via firstName (symbol, a field of const object SAML_STANDARD_CLAIMS))_
- `content/docs/frontend/data-objectstack.mdx`  _(via /app/:appId/bundle (route, bridged from symbol listOf — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via createObjectQLAdapterFactory (symbol, a top-level function), providerId (symbol, a field of interface SamlProviderScope))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx`  _(via firstName (symbol, a field of const object SAML_STANDARD_CLAIMS), lastName (symbol, a field of const object SAML_STANDARD_CLAIMS), providerId (symbol, a field of interface SamlProviderScope), INVALID_EMAIL (literal, a string literal in SSO_ACCOUNT_NOT_AN_ADDRESS))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via providerId (symbol, a field of interface SamlProviderScope))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via /app/:appId/bundle (route, bridged from symbol listOf — its route source's handler names it))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/register-sso-provider.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b4624440e699395d1929b1eb7d77f60b4185c481` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b5e1a7e57505dec92cab2dcaaf4697ec0104795c` — the merge of head `d8954d3c896485b8a287b657937540ff2d975445` into base `b4624440e699395d1929b1eb7d77f60b4185c481`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b5e1a7e57505dec92cab2dcaaf4697ec0104795c && git checkout b5e1a7e57505dec92cab2dcaaf4697ec0104795c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b4624440e699395d1929b1eb7d77f60b4185c481 d8954d3c896485b8a287b657937540ff2d975445 && git checkout -B drift-repro b4624440e699395d1929b1eb7d77f60b4185c481 && git merge --no-ff d8954d3c896485b8a287b657937540ff2d975445

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b4624440e699395d1929b1eb7d77f60b4185c481
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b4624440e699395d1929b1eb7d77f60b4185c481` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dedf965bef50f9e5dd1683bab517696a8880bc87`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-saml-standard-claims.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/objectql-adapter.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-sign-in-options.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-auth-instance.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-account-at-proven-domain.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-saml-refusal-cause.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/register-sso-provider.ts, content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx, .changeset/32146-saml-standard-claims.md + @better-auth/sso 1.7.12 dist/index.mjs (`computeProviderAuthenticationFingerprint`, `serializeCanonical`, `withoutSAMLPrivateKeys`, `safeJsonParse`)

I read `e9038583` in full, then the delta `e9038583...dedf965b` (sso.mdx, one new portal-first pin, and one changeset sentence; no runtime source).

### ① Derived judgments

- **The contract point: hidden mapping members and the vendor fingerprint.** The vendor binds an SP-initiated start to its ACS with `computeProviderAuthenticationFingerprint`: SHA-256 over `serializeCanonical`, which walks `Object.entries` (own enumerable keys, sorted), applied to `withoutSAMLPrivateKeys({...samlConfig})`. A member defined with `enumerable: false` is therefore invisible to the fingerprint, while the vendor's attribute read (`mapping.email` and so on) still sees it as a property. That is also the right meaning: the fingerprint guards the stored configuration between start and ACS, and these members are derived per request from the posted assertion, so they are not configuration. The author's ablation (enumerable → every SP-initiated sign-in refused) and the "groups-only stored mapping, SP-initiated still completes" pin measure both sides. The object the engine returned is never mutated (pinned), and the stored mapping and the get bridge are unchanged (CONTROL).
- **Pre-read of attribute names from an unverified response.** `samlAssertionAttributeNames` reads names only when the response holds exactly one `Assertion` element anywhere and no `EncryptedAssertion`, and caps the size at the vendor's read limit. That closes the signature-wrapping shape (two assertions → no names, so no fallback). The names only choose which attribute name the vendor reads. Every value still comes from the assertion the vendor validated, and a name not in it falls through to the old default. Scope is the AsyncLocalStorage of the ACS request, matched on `providerId`, so start, other providers and write echoes are untouched (pinned).
- **No-address refusal.** `refuseSsoAccountWithoutAddress` applies only to `create-user` from an SSO provider source, verification on or off, after the proven-domain rule. Existing accounts and non-SSO creation are unchanged (pinned for SAML IdP-initiated and SP-initiated, with an address CONTROL).
- **Delta.** sso.mdx now states the measured truth: two entries resolve to one address, and the second is refused `account_not_linked` and creates nothing until linked. The new portal-first pin (IdP-initiated first, then SP-initiated) shows one user and one account row. The changeset's BREAKING paragraph now names the `email`-vs-claim precedence (the S1 I raised before this head).
- **should-fix S1 (prose, changeset line 19).** "Both entries now resolve to the address in the `emailaddress` claim, so the second entry reaches the account the first one made, instead of creating another" contradicts the corrected sso.mdx and the new pin: the second entry is refused `account_not_linked` and reaches nothing until linked. The changeset ships as `CHANGELOG.md`, so make it say what sso.mdx says. A prose-only move keeps this PASS (Regen-provenance in the ACCEPT).
- nit N1: the hidden-member technique depends on vendor internals (spread + `Object.entries`). It is pinned both ways, so a vendor bump that changes it turns the SP-initiated pins red rather than failing silently. Keep a one-line note at the `hidden` helper naming the fingerprint function it relies on.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch`, `fix(auth)!`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with the widening in prose, a BREAKING paragraph, one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker. Correct for a non-protocol narrowing (AGENTS.md). `Metadata-protocol: none`, and `Skills-docs: none — reason` holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Vendor coupling** (`@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12 fingerprint): re-verify on any bump. The pins are the tripwire.
- No first-party composition registers a SAML or OIDC provider, so the narrowing lands on deployments (cloud / customer IdPs). The BREAKING text gives the remedy (map the email attribute or claim).
- CI at this head when read (20:05Z) is not complete. The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head, and the full dogfood battery owed by the narrowing arm must be green there.

### ④ Design judgment

#32146: an unmapped Entra ID or AD FS provider keyed its users on whatever NameID the entry produced, so the same person got two accounts (or an account keyed on an opaque id). Reading the standard claims for unset members, and refusing to create an account for a non-address, fixes both at the producer, without rewriting any stored mapping. Hiding the derived members from the fingerprint is the minimal way to add per-request inputs without breaking the vendor's start/ACS binding, and it is semantically correct. The design holds.
